plate_comment: Rail pressure sensor plausibility check that sets and clears fault 7 (P0191): while the coolant is at least 170 F, vehicle_speed_copy and fuel_demand_governor_output are at or below their limits (both 0 here), engine speed is within 25 rpm of the governor speed word (0x40aec2) and fuel_pressure_sensor is within 82 counts (4.0 MPa) of fuel_pressure_setpoint, it averages fuel_demand_computed over 150 passes and compares the average with an averaged expected fuel demand for the load (a table of four values, 16.9 to 25.2 mm3, chosen by the A/C clutch request and the alternator field duty, plus 13.6 mm3 for an automatic transmission in gear). Three consecutive tests with the same result set fault 7 (average not below the expected value, state 3) or clear it (state 2) and lock the verdict until the next start; called from cm848_runFuelPressureSensorPlausibilityMonitor. (was engine_protection_fuelCorrection_stateMachine)
evidence: Read in full and re-checked against the ROM: fault 7 (fault_detected_bits_0_to_15 mask 0x80) decodes to slot 151 = P0191, the same slot as fault 414 set by hpcr_checkRailPressureSensorBeforeStart. The wave 3 blocker (who else uses fuel_correction_ramp_state) is settled: xref shows only the init, the abort check, this check and the wrapper cm848_calibration_group26_load, so no other feature reads the state. Not fuel timing: all values are fuel quantities (cap 0x1700 = 5888 = 400 mm3). Constants in the dump: coolant 10880 = 170 F, vehicle speed limit 0, governor output limit 0, speed window 200 = 25 rpm, pressure window 82 counts (byte), 150 passes, 3 consecutive results; the table at 0x409ee2 is a byte-length word (8) plus the four entries 249 / 311 / 342 / 371 = 16.9 / 21.1 / 23.2 / 25.2 mm3 (the 0.5 mm3 first 'entry' of wave 3 is the length word); the addend 200 = 13.6 mm3 applies when transmission_type_cal is nonzero (3 here) and transmission_park_or_neutral_flag is 0. Four more gates: switch_input_state_bits[0] mask 8 clear, governor_fuel_active_flag 0, logical output 11 not requested, fault 397 not detected. The monitor is enabled on this truck: fault_feature_config_flags = 0x24 has bit 5. Established: what is computed and the fault it sets. Inferred: that a high averaged idle fuel demand points at the rail pressure sensor - that rests on the P0191 mapping only.

evidence: Read in full: its only job is this one monitor (state tests, the fault 7 bit, monitor-complete and pending bit 0x80000 handling); the single caller is cm848_periodicTaskGroup26_calibration8 (0xbd80).

plate_comment: Returns the next running average of the expected fuel demand for the rail pressure sensor plausibility check: (expected value x step count / 10 + entry param_1 of the expected fuel demand table + the in-gear fuel addend) x 10 / (step count + 10), capped at 5888 (the maximum fuel quantity). plate_comment: Start-up reset of the rail pressure setpoint-not-reached monitor: monitor state 0, accumulator and pass count zeroed (cm848_resetFuelPressureSetpointNotReachedAccumulator), fault 352 cleared and the monitor marked inactive; when protection_feature_flags bit 0x8000 is clear it also marks the monitor complete (clears bit 5 of fault_pending_flags, sets bit 5 of diagnostic_monitor_complete_bits). Decaying peak hold of fuel_demand_previous, used only in cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor (xref: word, 3 reads / 1 write). Each pass it takes fuel_demand_previous when that is above it or above its ceiling, or when the step is 0; otherwise it is limited to the ceiling (fuel_demand_base_offset minus the ceiling offset, floored at 0), lowered by the step and kept at or above fuel_demand_previous - so it never lies below the demand and falls linearly after a peak. It is one of the inputs of the governor output governor_proportional_gain (that output is fuel_demand_integrator_b_sum when this is below it, else the lower of this and fuel_demand_ramp_state). It is not an accumulator, so 'integrator' is wrong. Time-shared window 0x3F9800-0x3FDB30: xref_addr.py lists no user below 0x7F60 (the filter was checked on 0x3fee34 / 0x3fee3a, where it does find the boot users). No type change.

Read once, in cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor (xref: word, 1 read / 0 writes); ROM copy at 0x3ff6xx, outside the EEPROM range, so no _cal, and not cam timing. Per pass, while fuel_demand_previous is at or below both fuel_demand_decaying_peak (new name of fuel_demand_integrator_max, 0x3fa0fc) and its ceiling and the step is nonzero, the peak is limited to the ceiling (fuel_demand_base_offset minus the ceiling offset, floored at 0), lowered by the step and kept at or above fuel_demand_previous. The pair (step, ceiling offset) is chosen by fuel_pressure_setpoint - fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered against fuel_pressure_error_threshold (-307, signed): above it the 4 / 44 pair, otherwise the 2 / 29 pair (equality takes the 2 / 29 pair). This row is the step used above the threshold: 4 counts = 0.27 mm3 per pass.

State of the check: 0 not running, 1 averaging (all gates open), 2 passed (average below expected, fault 7 cleared), 3 failed (fault 7 set), 4 aborted by faults (cm848_abortFuelPressureSensorPlausibilityOnFaults). xref: word, 3 reads / 5 writes; users are the check, the wrapper, the abort check and the init only. Not a ramp and not a fuel correction.

Running average of fuel_demand_computed: (average x n / 10 + demand) x 10 / (n + 10), n = step count, capped at 5888; the first pass (n = 0) takes the demand itself. Compared with the expected average at step 150. xref: word, 2 reads / 2 writes (check, init).

Running average of the expected fuel demand (table value for the present load state plus the in-gear addend, averaged like the demand by cm848_calculateExpectedFuelDemandAverage): a fuel quantity of 16.9 to 38.8 mm3, not an injection timing. xref: word, 2 reads / 2 writes (check, averaging helper).

Fuel quantity added to the expected demand: the constant at 0x409ed8 (200 = 13.6 mm3) when transmission_type_cal is nonzero (3 = automatic here) and transmission_park_or_neutral_flag is 0 (in gear), else 0. xref: word, 1 read (the averaging helper) / 1 write (the check).

Byte-length word (8) followed by four expected fuel demands 249 / 311 / 342 / 371 (16.9 / 21.1 / 23.2 / 25.2 mm3): entry 1 = A/C clutch request (air_conditioning_clutch_request_byte mask 0x40) off and alternator_field_duty_target at or below the threshold, 2 = A/C on and duty at or below, 3 = A/C off and duty above, 4 = A/C on and duty above. The code reads entries 1-4 only, so the earlier 'five zones' and 0.5 mm3 are the length word. xref: 3 reads / 0 writes, ROM copy. Typed word: see the type note.

14080 = 55 percent of the 25600 duty scale: alternator_field_duty_target at or below it (or above) selects the expected table entry (xref: word, 4 reads / 0 writes, all in the check). Not a demand threshold and not about timing.

Passes counted while all gates stay open, 0 to 150 (limit at 0x409ede): the weight n of both averages, and a test is evaluated once at 150; set back to 0 whenever a gate closes. xref: word, 2 reads / 2 writes (check, init) plus the averaging helper read.

Consecutive tests whose average fuel demand was not below the expected value; at fuel_pressure_sensor_plausibility_result_count_limit (3) fault 7 is set (state 3). Reset to 0 when a test comes out the other way. xref: byte, 2 reads / 3 writes (check, init).

Consecutive tests whose average fuel demand was below the expected value; at fuel_pressure_sensor_plausibility_result_count_limit (3) fault 7 is cleared (state 2). Reset to 0 when a test comes out the other way. xref: byte, 2 reads / 3 writes (check, init).
3 in the dump: number of consecutive tests with the same result needed for a verdict. xref: byte, 2 reads / 0 writes, all in the check; ROM copy.

Set to 1 when a verdict (state 2 or 3) is reached; while set, a closing gate no longer resets the state, so the verdict holds until the init at the next start. xref: word, 2 reads / 2 writes (check, init). Time-shared window 0x3F9800-0x3FDB30: xref_addr.py lists no user below 0x7F60 (all users are the two plausibility functions). No type change proposed.

Set after a test result has been counted (evaluation only once per test: the check returns at once while it is set) and cleared with the state when a gate closes. xref: byte, 1 read / 3 writes (check, init). Time-shared window 0x3F9800-0x3FDB30: xref_addr.py lists no user below 0x7F60. No type change proposed.

Written once per cycle in cm848_evaluateInjectorDiagnostics with the 24-bit word (shifted left by 8) returned by cm848_readInjectorDiagnosticWord and passed to cm848_updateInjectorDiagnosticBits; xref: dword, 0 reads / 1 write, 1 function, so it is a stored copy of that word and has nothing to do with a cylinder period. Time-shared window: xref_addr.py lists no user below 0x7F60. No type change.

Per-cylinder-event cutout mask: engine_injectionAngle_updateCutoutAndTimingDemand ORs in 0x55 or 0xaa (alternate cylinder events, one injector group) when injector_diagnostic_bits_b / _c / _d or injection_check_flags request it, and the injection dispatch tests ((crank_sync_inhibit_flag | mask) >> (cylinder_event_index & 0x3f)) & 1; when its countdown ends it clears the mask or, past the shutdown cycle limit, clears a TPU-A channel 4 enable bit. cm848_evaluateInjectorDiagnostics passes it as the 'no healing' argument for classes c, b and d (they do not heal while a cutout is active). xref: word, 11 reads / 4 writes in 6 functions (cutout function 4r/3w, injector diagnostics 3r, per-cylinder timing scan 2r, three init / load functions).

Byte 6 of the 80-bit logical output request array at 0x40c080 (0x40c080 + 6; requests 48-55): cm848_setLogicalOutputRequest sets bit (n & 7) of byte n >> 3, so request 54 (called with 0x36 by cm848_updateFuelPressureFaultReactionRequests and cm848_applyFuelLimitsForFuelPressureFaults) is bit 0x40, the bit the injector diagnostics, the feedback circuit checks and the cutout scan test; bit 0x20 (request 53) is tested in 4 more places. xref: byte, 11 reads / 0 direct writes (the writes are indexed) in 8 functions. Same convention as logical_output_request_bits_8_to_15 (0x40c081); not the 'a' variant of protection_config_flags_b (0x3fd5a8), which is an unrelated EEPROM word.

No single subject, so no name: its 25 reads (xref: word, 0 writes, 20 functions, none below 0x7F60 although it sits in the time-shared window) test bit 0 (1 site, together with fuel_demand_mode_index), bit 1 (the rpm-table fuel limiter, 1 site), bit 2 (10 sites, e.g. with protection_mode_changed_flag), bit 3 (the transmission gear 1 / 2 and lockup logic, 9 tests), bit 4 (cruise switches learned, 2 sites), bit 5 (sensor deviation check pending, 1 site) and bit 15 (cruise engaged, 1 site). EEPROM mirror (EEPROM 0x126), so a rename needs _cal; the honest name is a generic subject-free one, probably for the whole word group 0x3fd5a0-0x3fd5b6 (they may be one feature configuration block - not checked), which is a family decision, not a single-row one. 'protection' is the subject of none of these bits.

10880 = 170 F (1/64 F per count): the check runs only with coolant_temp at or above it. Width: xref_addr.py says word (1 read / 0 writes), and the load is lha, a signed compare with the temperature. ROM copy, outside 0x3fd482-0x3feec1, so no _cal.

82 counts = 4.0 MPa: largest |fuel_pressure_sensor - fuel_pressure_setpoint| for which the check runs. Width: xref_addr.py says byte (1 read / 0 writes, lbz at an odd address); a word peek here gives 21047 = 0x5237, which is this byte (0x52) plus the first byte of the next word 0x409ed6, so read it as one byte.

0 in the dump: the check runs only while fuel_demand_governor_output is not above it. Width: xref_addr.py says word (1 read / 0 writes), lhz.

text: Fault decode re-checked against the ROM image (slot = u16 at 0x5985a + 2 x fault, code = BCD word at 0x5b57c + 2 x slot): 57 / 58 / 60 = slots 162 / 163 / 164 = P1221 / P1222 / P1223, 59 = slot 158 (code word 0000), 69 / 70 / 71 = the same three codes, 303 = P0088, 304 = P0193, 305 = P0192, 333 = P0251, 408 / 409 = P0148, and 264 / 265 / 270 / 273 / 276 / 279 / 282 / 285 / 290 / 315-317 / 323 / 324 / 352 = slot 170 (no code), as wave 3 said. New: fault 7 AND fault 414 both decode to slot 151 = P0191, so P0191 has two detectors: the running plausibility check (fault 7, cm848_checkFuelPressureSensorPlausibilityByFuelDemand) and the before-start sensor voltage check (fault 414, hpcr_checkRailPressureSensorBeforeStart); the running check is aborted while fault 414 is detected.

Out of group, not read in full: cm848_selectTorqueLimit (0x1fd94), cm848_initTorqueLimitDefaults and the torque_limit_* / torque_fuel_* family are an ENGINE SPEED limit arbitration, not torque. Evidence: the arbitrated result torque_limit_arb_t.fuel_minimum (lowest of the limit sources 2-16) is compared directly with engine_rpm_state_t.current_rpm in cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit (0x20554), which cuts the fuel limit in proportion to the speed above it; every value is rpm x 8: default torque_limit_fuel_minimum (0x3fd814) 30000 = 3750 rpm, torque_fuel_limit_abs_max_cal 28000 = 3500 rpm (final cap), torque_limit_bypass_threshold_cal 6800 = 850 rpm (floor), torque_limit_fuel_reference_init 25600 = 3200 rpm, governor_speed_limit_output 6000 = 750 rpm; the converter function cm848_monitorConverterSlipAndFuelLimit feeds source 13 with an rpm-scaled table value. Suggest renaming the whole family at once (engine_speed_limit_*, cm848_selectTorqueLimit -> cm848_selectEngineSpeedLimit). 0x3fd814 itself is in the EEPROM mirror (so it needs _cal; xref: word, 29 reads in 15 functions, none below 0x7F60) and in the time-shared window, so it is not renamed here.

CSV comment to replace for fault_reaction_request_bits (0x40b8a0): 'Fault reaction mask built by cm848_updateFuelPressureFaultReactionRequests from the per-fault masks of faults 317, 290, 324, 408 and 352 (bit 3 of the previous value is kept): bit 0 caps governor_fuel_limit_source at fault_reaction_fuel_limit, bit 1 caps the engine speed limit fuel_pressure_fault_engine_speed_limit_working at fault_reaction_engine_speed_limit, bit 2 caps fuel_pressure_setpoint at fuel_pressure_setpoint_fault_reaction_cap (4095 = no cap here), bit 3 requests logical output 54. A nonzero value also ramps the speed limit down, blocks cruise and zeroes the PCI fuel level. In this calibration only fault 352 has a mask (5 = bits 0 and 2) and its caps (5888 and 4095) have no effect. (was cold_start_qualifier_flag) (Medium confidence)'. Type notes, no change proposed: 0x409530 fuel_pressure_too_high_count_limit is typed word but its only access is one lbz (xref: byte, 1 read / 0 writes) and 0x409531 has no access at all (value 0, probably padding of the ROM block), so it should be a byte and 0x409531 needs no row. 0x409ee2 (fuel_pressure_sensor_plausibility_expected_fuel_demand_table) is a byte-length word plus four entries (word[5], the first being the length), not a five-zone table. The 16 + 13 interpolation state words at 0x3fd0ca-0x3fd102 and the 7 + 1 words at 0x3fb6cc-0x3fb6da are in the time-shared window, so no array typing is proposed. 0x409a6d is read as a word at an odd address because of how the ROM block is packed (no change).

cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor tail, read for the four cam_timing_correction_* rows (function name kept, the rest of its 565 lines not verified): fuel_demand_integrator_max (0x3fa0fc, used only in this function) is a decaying peak hold of fuel_demand_previous (it jumps up to a higher demand and otherwise falls by the step, never below fuel_demand_previous), not an accumulator, so it is renamed fuel_demand_decaying_peak above and the four new row names are built on that name. The output governor_proportional_gain is then fuel_demand_integrator_b_sum when that is above the peak, else the lower of the peak and fuel_demand_ramp_state (a rate-limited ceiling that starts at 0x1700). The sibling names fuel_demand_integrator_b / fuel_demand_integrator_b_sum / fuel_demand_integrator_b_limit (the rpm-drop fuel term) were not checked for the same doubt.

Facts for this truck's image: fault_feature_config_flags (0x3fd5b6) = 0x24, so bit 5 (the plausibility check enable) is set and the check runs; transmission_type_cal = 3 (automatic), so the 13.6 mm3 in-gear addend applies while transmission_park_or_neutral_flag is 0; the four second-limit rows are 20000 / 20000 / 30400 / 20000 = 2500 / 2500 / 3800 / 2500 rpm (only the 3800 rpm one, above the 3750 rpm default, can never lower the speed limit), so a registered fault 304 / 305 / 264 / 333 / 303 feeds a 2500 rpm limit into the speed limit arbitration (the arbitration result itself was not traced to the end), next to the 883 = 60 mm3 fuel limits (limp home mask 156 = faults 333 / 304 / 305 / 303).
